title: GlossaryTerm
description: A defined business term with synonyms, classification tags, authority links to external vocabularies, and links to related terms.

specVersion.description: Spec version of this document, e.g. "2.0.0".

name.description: The canonical name of the term (e.g. "Date of Birth").

definition.description: The authoritative definition of the term.

synonyms.description: Alternative names or abbreviations for this term (e.g. ["DOB", "birth date"]).

tags.description: Classification tags (e.g. PII category tags) applied to this term.

authorityLinks.description: Links to definitions of this term in external authority systems.

relatedTerms.description: URNs of related GlossaryTerms. Pattern: urn:srcos:glossary:<id>

partOfSpeech.description: Tesnière grain: noun-phrase (NP) = an estate ENTITY/actant; verb-phrase (VP) = an ACTION/service. Optional; required-in-effect once status is 'approved' (validator).

status.description: Lifecycle. A 'draft' term may be partially aligned (capture in flight); an 'approved' term MUST be fully aligned across all three methods (validator, fail-closed).

alignment.description: Alignment across the three methods that make a term governance-usable: (1) formal ontology class; (2) NP↔VP vector link in the sovereign space; (3) estate entity/service binding.

ontologyClassRef.description: Method 1 — the formal ontology/KKO class this term is captured as.

vectorLink.description: Method 2 — the semantic vector link to a peer term (NP↔VP), in the SAME sovereign space as EmbeddingRequest (model + dimension pinned by const).

peerRef.description: The peer term (an NP links to a VP and vice versa).

estateBinding.description: Method 3 — the real estate entity/service that IMPLEMENTS this term. NP→entity, VP→service|action (validator).

relations.description: Typed relations to other terms / ontology classes / estate refs, over a CLOSED predicate set (RDF/RDFS/SKOS/FOAF patterns) so a reasoner can derive dependencies + constraints and cross-check them against the blast-radius graph and the neurosymbolic domain. Inverse pairs (is-type/has-type, is-member/has-member, skos:broader/skos:narrower) must reciprocate; skos:related is symmetric; is-a (subsumption) must be acyclic.
